findings.title: Reject non-object JSON records in the completion gate
findings.trigger: A required status, boundary, provenance, or base-status file contains valid non-object JSON such as null or [].
findings.execution_path: completion_gate._read parses the value and returns None without adding a reason. Each subsequent record check runs only when its value is not None, so the required check is skipped.
findings.consequence: The standalone completion gate reports pass and exits 0 without a complete status, verified boundary, established provenance, or required cross-grade. The separate readiness predicate still rejects a missing boundary, but the documented completion gate is independently fail-open.
findings.evidence: With valid inspection metadata requiring a cross-grade and all four other records supplied as JSON null, _completion_gate_main printed gate=pass, reasons=[] and returned 0. Existing gate tests cover missing files, mismatched objects, and symlinks, but omit valid JSON of the wrong type.
findings.suggested_fix: Append a named validation failure whenever a required record is not a JSON object. Add parameterized tests for null, arrays, strings, numbers, and booleans in every required record, including base-status.

findings.title: Keep inspection grading bound to the verified main checker
findings.trigger: The operator or another process edits the checker/schema or switches the harness checkout while the container review is running.
findings.execution_path: establish_trusted_main verifies the checkout before launching Codex. After the potentially 1800-second review, _execute_inspection checks the PR's remote head but directly executes checker_argv, which points to REPO_ROOT/tests/codex_report_status.py. It never repeats audit_inputs or compares the recorded hashes. Cross-grading occurs only when the reviewed PR changed an audited input.
findings.consequence: A different checker can grade the report while provenance still claims trusted main. Switching the checkout to an untrusted branch can execute that branch's Python on the host; even an ordinary concurrent edit can produce completion under unrecorded grading rules.
findings.evidence: The trusted _execute_reserved path explicitly re-audits and compares inputs immediately before grading; the new inspection path omits that safeguard. Plan 85.1-06 explicitly requests the same re-audit. An in-memory orchestration check confirmed that the checkout checker is invoked after simulated state change without calling audit_inputs. Existing orchestration tests mock provenance and checker output but do not mutate audited inputs during review.
findings.suggested_fix: Always materialize and execute the checker/schema from the verified main_sha in a private directory retained through grading. Also reject changes to recorded audited inputs before reporting completion. Add a regression that replaces the checker/schema during the mocked review and proves the replacement is never executed.
findings.hypothesis: Actual concurrent checkout replacement was not executed in the read-only sandbox. Static tracing and mocked orchestration establish the missing revalidation and mutable checker path; the host-execution consequence requires that path to change during the review.

limitations: Full pytest was not rerun because this sandbox is read-only and the suite requires temporary files. Harness evidence for the exact head reports 3022 passed, 1 skipped, and exit 0.
No live Docker, Codex authentication, GitHub API, or network validation was performed.
The completion-gate reproduction substituted record bytes at the safe-reader boundary; it exercised the real parser and gate without writing files.
The concurrent-checker scenario was traced and checked with mocked orchestration, not a real checkout switch.
Several initial read outputs were truncated; affected scope was subsequently inspected through smaller reads.
